$comment: SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0. Portable verification extension 0.2.0 (proposal), written against Core v1.3 rev. 11 and reference files 5.2.0, with signatures 0.2.0 and anchoring 0.2.0 for a signed entry. Binds only an implementation that says it uses this extension.
title: Portable verification export
description: Sealed decision records exported so that another party can check them. The export sits beside the records: it points to them and carries their sealed bytes, and never adds a field to a record. A document that names a member twice, at any depth, is not read.

issuer_checkpoint.description: A checkpoint supplied by the issuer. It comes from the same source as the export, so it cannot show that no entry is missing.

derived_digest.description: SHA-256 of the covered bytes of a derived representation. It is never presented as the original seal.

oneOf.description: A derived representation: linked to the original seal, never carrying it as its own.

covered_representation.description: How the covered bytes were produced: the original bytes, or a canonical form fixed by a named specification.

specification_ref.description: A reference to a specification that fixes every byte of the canonical form.

covered_bytes_b64.description: The exact bytes that were hashed into the seal, unchanged, in padded base64.

reason_ref.description: The decision_id of the redaction event or of the disposition record.

seal_hash.description: The record's seal_hash (Core §5.1(3), §6.2), in lowercase hex. A seal stored in another encoding of the same 32 bytes is carried as lowercase hex.

seal_field_handling.description: seal_hash_absent: the covered bytes do not contain seal_hash. seal_hash_zeroed: they contain seal_hash with every character of its value replaced by the character 0, which keeps the length of the stored value. Other placeholders, such as an empty string or null, are not covered.

affirmation_record_covered.description: Whether the covered bytes include affirmation_record: a statement about the bytes, not a rule about what they must include.

record_ref.description: The decision_id of the record of the transformation, such as a migration record (Core §6.2.3.2), where there is one.

chain.description: link(i) = SHA-256(link(i-1) || digest(i)) over 32-byte raw values, with 32 zero bytes before the first entry; digest(i) is the entry's seal_hash or derived_digest. previous_link is link(i-1), in lowercase hex. The chain binds the seals and their order, not which record each seal belongs to.

signature.description: The issuer's signature of the entry: the signatures 0.2.0 organisation seal of kind record, over this entry's decision_id and its digest (seal_hash for an original, derived_digest for a derived representation) and sealed_at, under the signed-bytes rule that profile names. The verifier builds the signed bytes from the entry itself, so a signature moved to another entry, or made over the original's seal for a derived entry, fails. The key comes from the verifier's own trust policy, never from the export.

key_ref.description: A reference to the issuer's key, in role organisation in the verifier's trust policy.

signed_bytes_ref.description: Where the exact signed bytes are defined: the signatures 0.2.0 organisation seal.

sealed_at.description: The time the issuer states, signed. It is the stated time for the key's state, and never time assurance for the record.
